messages:
Zoe: Odd failure during magnet-14b-int8 bringup. We saw a consistent 3-token drift when async prefetch merges a freshly-prefilled fp16 shard with an int8 hotshard. Prefill was 88k; drift shows up within the next 5 tokens.

Manu: Can you paste the minimal run + snippet?

Zoe: run id: async-prefetch-merge-2025-08-09-a
Command:
```bash
./serve_local --model magnet-14b-mixed --ctx 200000 --prefill tests/long_88k.txt --kv-prefetch async --seed 9
```
Log snippet:
```text
[02:15:01] prefill OK tokens=88000
[02:15:17] async-prefetch: grabbed shard-2 (fp16) for indices [65536..86000]
[02:15:18] merged hotshard int8 shard-5 into active map
[02:15:19] continuation token expected=' the' got=' tha' (offset +3)
```

Priya: Huh. Mixed-precision prefetched shards shouldn't be merged without normalization. Are we normalizing RoPE multipliers across shard boundaries?

Zoe: Apparently not. The prefetch path stores raw token-level rot_offsets from whoever serialized the shard. When warmhot merge happens, the active kernel assumes a single rot_multiplier table and applies a per-token rotary that mismatches the prefills. Only occurs with async prefetch + mixed precision.

Infra Bot: job async-prefetch-merge-2025-08-09-a recorded (commit e2b7f4). Artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/async-prefetch/merge/1876543210/artifacts.tar.gz

Manu: Can you repro with a synthetic that toggles precision per-shard? I want to see if the problem is rot_offset serialization or the merge path.

Zoe: Minimal repro in tests/repro/mixed_prefetch_merge.py. It creates two shard files (fp16, int8) with different rope_scale histories then triggers an async merge. Repro flags: --force-merge --shuffle-order. Deterministic: mismatch within 3 tokens every run.

Priya: I instrumented rotary.apply and saw that applied_rot_offset sequence before merge = [...,65534,65535,65536,65537,...] but after merge the kernel sees [...,65534, 65535, 1, 2,...] for the same global positions. Looks like one shard's rot_offset was serialized relative to its local base and not rebased to the global token count during merge.

Manu: So a rebasing bug. When we hydrate a prefetched shard we must add the shard_base to the stored offsets. If we forget, the per-token multipliers wrap/shift and cause drift. Why only int8?

Zoe: Good question. I think int8 hotshard uses compact encoding that stores delta-of-deltas and relies on an external `base` field to reconstruct. The fp16 shard stored absolute offsets. Merge path assumed both were absolute and didn't apply base for int8. Hence the shift. So mixed precision + async prefetch exposes the mismatch.

QA: Adding regression. Tests/longcontext will get a new case: mixed-shard-merge at prefills [65k,88k,120k] with async prefetch enabled. Fail if any token differs from fp16 baseline.

Manu: Quick mitigation: block async prefetch when we detect heterogeneous precision until we fix rebasing logic. Also add an assert in shard-hydrate that verifies applied_rot_offset >= shard_base && applied_rot_offset < shard_base + shard_len. If violated, fail-hot and fallback to full-replay.

Zoe: Opened PR #ML-1350: fix rebasing during hydrate + add unit test for mixed encodings, plus a defensive checksum in the shard header. Also added warning logs when a prefetched shard's encoding != active encoding.

Infra Bot: PR #ML-1350 CI results: broken on one test; failing case indicates we missed a legacy int8 compact path. Artifact: s3://redwood-ci/pr-1350/logs.tar.gz

Priya: I'll follow up to patch the legacy path. Long-term: standardize shard serialization schema with explicit fields: version, precision, base_offset, checksum. No implicit assumptions.

Manu: For onboarding safety: mark P1, add canary rule to Dedicated onboarding to disable async prefetch for mixed-precision models until PR merged and canary passes. Also add a nightly job that runs mixed-shard-merge smoke with 88k prefill.

Zoe: Thanks team. I'll leave the repro env up (ssh dev-prefetch-1) and attach the minimal repro + prefetched shard artifacts in the run. Please ping me if you want to run bisection or try a patch. :mag:
